details: Implementation Plan I have what I need for the plan. Main findings: the review workflow is at 472,478 bytes, so the failure-path step bodies have to move into `scripts/`. A probe-free classifier could be spoofed by text in a PR. The Claude path logs `all_accounts_failed`, not `all_gated`. **Implementation plan — Issue: classify model-provider outages as `provider_unavailable`, pause and resume automatically (re-issue of #5773)** Planning ref: `main`. The planning context recorded `e735f99d00788132f6ae83674e29caa378dacc6b`; the isolated snapshot here reports `f7bca8d`. There is no integration-branch metadata, so there is no branch mismatch. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends workflow_failure_heal.py (identical-failure fingerprint cap, failure marker, autofix reporter) and the review_security_hold_sweep.py scheduled-sweep pattern Scope-mode justification: This plan implements the pipeline side of #5773 as the clarification bound it: Q1:B (every repo), Q2:A (a per-repo `ai:provider-outage` tracker issue), Q3:A (Claude pool capacity gets an alert only). The Claude-session parts retired in #6176 are excluded. The fix is at the root: an outage failure gets its own reason, so the cap never counts it and no block label is applied. Because of that, no new `workflow_dispatch` bypass input is needed. A new input would also have caused `startup_failure` on this PR's own review runs (agents.md, the "internal-review.yml must not forward a with: input" rule). Per the Boil-the-Lake rule I include the extra pieces the plan would otherwise defer: closing out the Claude pool capacity alert, the release re-run reporting, and marker-gated label clean-up. Each costs little and adds no new dependency or external interface (§6: Correctness ahead of Speed). --- ## Automation / wiring (§20.E) - **New script:** `scripts/provider_outage.py`. It is a helper called only by existing automation, never run by hand. It is not a supervisor and not long-running; it does one bounded pass per invocation, like `scripts/review_security_hold_sweep.py` and `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py`, neither of which has a registry entry. So no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry is needed. - **Extended scripts:** `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh`, `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`, `scripts/ai_engine.sh`, `scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh`. - **New step scripts** (§24 split pattern, because `review_autofix.yml` is at 472,478 bytes against the 480,000 guard): `scripts/review_autofix_step_assemble_failure_evidence.sh`, `scripts/review_autofix_step_failure_comment.sh`, `scripts/review_autofix_step_provider_outage_record.sh`. - **Where it is wired (all in this PR):** - `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, codex-agent failure path. Every PR event goes through it, in this repo and in consumers via `@stable`. - `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`, schedule `*/30 * * * *`. A new probe/resume step runs before "Enumerate open PRs and dispatch internal-review.yml". - `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`, existing schedule `17 * * * *`. A new sibling job `provider-outage-resume` is added, modelled on `security-hold-sweep`. - `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` (`workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`, `repository_dispatch`): release-run outage skip. - **Supervisor:** none required. - **DB work:** none. The gate pattern used is "already applied" sentinels: tracker body and comment markers, with idempotent resume bookkeeping. --- ## 1. Functions and modules ### `scripts/provider_outage.py` (pattern: `review_security_hold_sweep.py`) The module docstring states the batching contract (§14). - **`provider_failure_status(texts) -> {"provider": "openrouter", "status": "402|401|429|5xx"} | None`** - Ported from the classifier in `security_audit.sh` (lines 163–176): `payment required|insufficient credits` → 402; `rate limit` → 429; a status regex for 401/402/429/5xx; plus JSON provider error bodies `"error":{"code":}`. - It only reads pipeline-emitted lines: reviewer-slot logs, summariser logs, `editor_stage_stderr.txt`, `resolver_stage_stderr.txt`, `collect_metadata_stderr.txt`, and the judge's stderr. - It ignores lines prefixed `UNTRUSTED_DATA:` and diff-hunk lines starting with `+` / `-`. - **`probe_openrouter(key, model) -> {"outcome": "up|down|unknown", "status": ...}`** - Step 1: `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key` (`Authorization: Bearer`). A 401 means down/401; `limit_remaining <= 0` means down/402. - Step 2: `POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": , "max_tokens": 1, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "OK"}]}`. Status 402/401/429/5xx means down. 2xx means up. Network error or timeout means unknown. - 15 s timeout. The key is never printed. Results are cached in `--probe-cache` so one run probes at most once. - **`classify(log_files, probe_cache)`** prints `reason=provider_unavailable provider=openrouter status=402` only when the evidence matches **and** the live probe returns down. Otherwise it prints `reason=none`. Fail-open: a missing key or an unknown probe result gives `none`, which is today's behaviour. - **`find_trackers(kind)`** - One `GET repos/{r}/issues?labels=ai:provider-outage&state=open&per_page=100`. - It keeps only issues authored by the GH_PAT login (`GET /user`) that carry the body marker. - It ignores pull requests. - **`open_tracker(kind, provider, status, release_run=None, alert_out)`** - If a trusted tracker of that kind is already open, it does no write (`outcome=already_open`). - Otherwise it creates the issue with the label and title (`AI Provider Outage` for an outage, `AI Claude Pool Capacity` for capacity), sleeps 5 s, and lists again. - If its own issue is the lowest-numbered one, it writes the alert text to `alert_out` (`alert=1`). Otherwise it closes its own duplicate silently. - A release run is recorded as an append-only tracker comment ``, not as a body PATCH, so there are no lost updates. - **`mark_label(item, pr, head, run)`** posts `` on the item. - **`sweep(...)`**, the scheduled entry point. It writes `paused` / `capacity_open` / `recovered` to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`: 1. If no trusted tracker is open: `paused=false`, done (one GET). 2. If an outage tracker is open: probe. Down or unknown means `paused=true`, done. Unknown fails closed for the pause, so outage runs are not wasted. 3. If the probe is up, resume: - Read the resume marker from the tracker body (``). - Batched GraphQL over open PRs: 50 per page, `headRefOid`, `comments(last:100)`.
